correctness.rationale: The stationary renewal age is exactly survival/mean; overlap of tensor-product Rabi states is cos^N, with binomial Fourier coefficients. Fourier age transform is derived by Fubini and bounded O(1/k), yielding square summability; dominated convergence on central-binomial ratios plus Parseval gives the prefactor for every finite-mean clock. A unit-modulus expectation equals one iff the interarrival lies on the Rabi full-period lattice; mean feasibility and a two-point epsilon/one-period construction prove the exact attained/unattained infimum. Partial fractions yield the Poisson constant. A standalone standard-library checker passes 51 finite checks; these diagnostics do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-spin purity formula and general renewal spectral theory are already implied by 2022 primary work and are explicitly not claimed to be new. After full-text comparisons, the assessed added theorem is the universal arbitrary-renewal many-body square-root purity law with exact L2 prefactor and the complete fixed-mean attainment/nonattainment classification. Relevant prior records on qubit concurrence, local qubit coherence and global rate Fisher information address different quantities; remaining unindexed antecedents are a genuine risk.
residual_risks: A generic purity formula, including Eq. (42) in arXiv:2209.05643, is known and already subsumes the finite-N algebra; thermodynamic asymptotics and constrained optimizers are the sole asserted advances.
Further specialist literature might have already derived this particular clock-phase L2 asymptotic and optimizer, despite the targeted searches and full-text checks.
Independent literature/prior-art assessment remains necessary for publication priority.

value.rationale: The exact thermodynamic purity coefficient determines how a single shared random clock generates subextensive ensemble mixing across an arbitrarily large noninteracting quantum register. A physically natural mean-reset-time budget exhibits a rigorous sharp attainment transition: full phase-dephasing is feasible at and above one Rabi period but below this threshold only approached by an increasingly singular mixture of near-zero and one-period intervals. This distinction matters to protocol optimization with timing constraints and is not merely a numerical special case.
